comments.author: ajss
comments.why: Talk on anti-patterns in system design.
comments.text: Along a similar line, I love Stuart Halloway's talk on Narcissistic Design - [VIDEO] Prefer APIs over data. Start with DSLs. Always connect (and never enqueue). Create abstractions for information. Use static typing across subsystem boundaries. Put language semantics on the wire. Write lots of unit tests. Leverage context. Update information in place.

comments.author: blacktriangle
comments.story: SQLBolt – Interactive lessons and exercises to learn SQL
comments.why: Covers anti-patterns including why SQL is only a DSL.
comments.text: [VIDEO] This talk goes into many anti-patterns, but he gets to the real problem with SQL, that it is ONLY a DSL and lacks either an API or a fundamental information model to program against. Composability when working with a DSL is a nightmare. I also have been moving away from ORM to directly writing SQL, but lets be honest about the reasons that programmers are wary of working directly with SQL as they are legitimate issues.
